sources.title: JPL planetary satellite discovery circumstances
sources.evidence: Live Saturn section contains 293 objects; names, IAU numerals, provisional designations and references individually reconciled.

sources.title: JPL planetary satellite mean orbital elements
sources.evidence: 291 Saturn entries individually matched; includes SAT459 targets. Mean elements describe source solutions, not an implemented or validated runtime fit.
sources.scope: All Saturn rows except S/2009 S1 and S/2009 S2

sources.title: JPL planetary satellite ephemerides
sources.evidence: 284 Saturn entries individually matched; Skathi appears as Skadi (627). Seven newest irregulars and two ring moonlets absent here; SAT458 entries are superseded by SAT459 where actual comments establish membership.
sources.scope: 284 explicit table matches; source inventory omissions recorded per row

sources.title: JPL planetary satellite physical parameters
sources.evidence: Read finite body list and radius/GM metadata. A radius entry is not measured triaxial axes or a released shape mesh.
sources.scope: Saturn major satellites actually listed; no blanket physical coverage for 293

sources.title: NAIF generic Saturn satellite kernels
sources.evidence: Read available releases; followed actual SAT459 and SAT480 comments without downloading binary kernels.
sources.scope: Released satellite ephemerides, with per-target membership below

sources.title: JPL SAT459 actual SPK comments
sources.evidence: 18 explicit satellite name/code mappings 65286–65303; supersedes the lagging grouped summary. Source time coverage is not an accuracy guarantee.

sources.title: JPL SAT480 actual SPK comments
sources.evidence: July 2026 release fits Cassini imaging for S/2009 S2, code 65304, nominal JED 1950–2050. Radius-axis and GM zeros mean unmodeled, not measured zero size.

sources.title: Denk et al. 2018: The Irregular Satellites of Saturn
sources.evidence: Read Table 3 and individual-target discussion: 25 Cassini-observed irregulars, 23 numerical minimum equatorial ratios, no ratio for Narvi/Kari. The ratios use a uniform-albedo reference ellipsoid.
sources.scope: Exact Table 3 membership and numeric data recorded per row

sources.title: Denk and Mottola 2019: Studies of irregular satellites I
sources.evidence: Research record for Cassini-derived rotation and shape constraints; detailed source values cross-checked against the accessible chapter and author target pages.
sources.scope: Cassini irregular photometry; target-specific scope in 2018 Table 3

sources.title: Denk et al. 2026 review of irregular and minor moons
sources.evidence: Read irregular-moon section and footnote 47: 13 convex models calculated, associated papers in preparation. This does not establish a released native mesh inventory. Convex inversion does not recover concavities.
sources.scope: Cassini irregular model availability; not evidence of surface data for every new discovery

sources.title: Denk irregular Saturn moons research portal
sources.evidence: Read physical/observational inventories and links; 122-target physical table is a bounded older inventory, not all 293 satellites. Introductory population wording does not override JPL.
sources.scope: Individual membership reconciled against 122-target table and 25-target Cassini table

sources.title: Denk 122-irregular physical and orbit table
sources.evidence: UTF-16 table decoded and all 122 numeric rows parsed. H and approximate diameter recorded separately from unmeasured axes; empty rotation/lightcurve cells retained as unknown in this product.
sources.scope: 122 exact designations/codes; 146 newer irregulars individually checked outside this inventory

sources.title: Cassini irregular-moon observation planning records
sources.evidence: Read author-released observation sequence inventory to distinguish instrument observations from extracted spectra or registered maps.
sources.scope: Cassini irregular observation sequences; Table 3 membership used for physical claims

sources.title: PDS Cassini Saturn satellite shape models V1.0
sources.evidence: Released 2018 Thomas plate models for exactly eleven named targets. None of the provisional irregulars or tiny Methone/Pallene/Polydeuces/Anthe/Aegaeon have a deliverable in this bundle.
sources.scope: Pan; Daphnis; Atlas; Prometheus; Pandora; Epimetheus; Janus; Telesto; Calypso; Helene; Hyperion

sources.title: PDS Cassini small-satellite shape inventory
sources.evidence: Read bundle target inventory and body-document routes; existing source pins separately identify each used plate model.
sources.scope: Pan; Daphnis; Atlas; Prometheus; Pandora; Epimetheus; Janus; Telesto; Calypso; Helene; Hyperion

sources.title: Cassini ISS PDS Ring-Moon Systems archive
sources.evidence: Mission camera products require per-image geometry, filters, native resolution and coverage; observation existence does not imply a global map. Existing packages preserve such provenance.
sources.scope: Cassini-observed Saturn targets; exact product evidence in existing package source or cited papers

sources.title: Hedman et al.: photometric properties of Saturn small moons
sources.evidence: Measured-axis and disk-integrated photometry study; existing package tables distinguish observed axes, uncertain albedo-derived size and Cassini frame registration limits.
sources.scope: Small inner moons, especially Methone, Pallene, Polydeuces, Anthe and Aegaeon

sources.title: NAIF generic planetary constants PCK00011
sources.evidence: Body-specific axes and radii used by existing packages; some small-body constants are estimates. They are not global relief models.
sources.scope: Existing regular Saturn packages and their explicit NAIF codes

sources.title: PDS Cassini topography release inventory
sources.evidence: Live inventory has 2025 Mimas/Tethys/Dione/Rhea bundles and Phoebe release; no Enceladus/Iapetus SPC bundle present in this checked directory.
sources.scope: Explicit release membership, not a universal claim of missing models

sources.title: Weirich et al. 2025 Mimas SPC model
sources.evidence: Released body-specific SPC topography and assessment products. Mimas is already used; Tethys/Dione/Rhea current recipes remain spheres with elevation textures.

sources.title: Weirich et al. 2025 Tethys SPC model
sources.evidence: Released body-specific SPC topography and assessment products. Mimas is already used; Tethys/Dione/Rhea current recipes remain spheres with elevation textures.

sources.title: Tethys SPC data inventory
sources.evidence: Global and regional release directories listed. Global subdirectory fetch returned HTTP 403; individual mesh byte identity still to establish.

sources.title: Weirich et al. 2025 Dione SPC model
sources.evidence: Released body-specific SPC topography and assessment products. Mimas is already used; Tethys/Dione/Rhea current recipes remain spheres with elevation textures.

sources.title: Dione SPC data inventory
sources.evidence: Global and regional release directories listed. Global subdirectory fetch returned HTTP 403; individual mesh byte identity still to establish.

sources.title: Weirich et al. 2025 Rhea SPC model
sources.evidence: Released body-specific SPC topography and assessment products. Mimas is already used; Tethys/Dione/Rhea current recipes remain spheres with elevation textures.

sources.title: Rhea SPC data inventory
sources.evidence: Actual rhea_128_o.obj and rhea_512_o.obj listed alongside radius and assessment grids.

sources.title: Schenk and McKinnon 2024 Enceladus controlled mosaic
sources.evidence: Controlled 100 m mosaic and companion 200 m terrain grid; registered to a reference ellipsoid with semi-axes 256.2 × 251.4 × 248.6 km. Source grid spacing is not uniform measurement accuracy.

sources.title: Enceladus Cassini 200 m terrain model
sources.evidence: Companion DEM is already pinned and used as an elevation lens in the inspected package; direct web page unresolved during this pass, mosaic metadata and package provenance identify the grid.

sources.title: Weirich et al. EPSC-DPS2025-115
sources.evidence: Describes Enceladus and Iapetus SPC products as forthcoming; checked live archive does not establish either release.

sources.title: Weller 2026 Titan Cassini near-infrared mosaic
sources.evidence: Inspected package pins 937.994 nm map, 702 m grid, 23048 × 11524. DOI resolution was unavailable in this research pass; current source metadata reviewed at implementation commit.

sources.title: Cassini mission-end Titan RADAR MIDR S00
sources.evidence: Existing package preserves observed SAR/HiSAR swaths and exact no-data; map backscatter is not optical color or height.

sources.title: Corlies et al. 2017 Titan topography and shape
sources.evidence: Global interpolation joins sparse topographic measurements covering about nine percent of the surface; measured coverage and interpolated model must remain separate.

sources.title: Cornell released Titan Corlies topography
sources.evidence: Actual alt_32PPD.cub, dtm_32PPD.cub, sar_32PPD.cub, topo_4PPD.cub and topo_4PPD_interp.cub listed. Did not download 26 MB data archive or validate map units/no-data.

sources.title: 2019 Titan VIMS/ISS color composite
sources.evidence: Existing source review records author-filled neighboring color and manual seam removal without an observed-color validity mask; not ready as an observed global color lens.

sources.title: Zubarev and Nadezhdina 2025 Hyperion mapping
sources.evidence: Paper reports 50 m global mapping and terrain model with a revised frame. No downloadable map/DEM file identity was established in this bounded search.

sources.title: PDS Gaskell Phoebe shape model
sources.evidence: Native Phoebe vertex/facet model already used by existing package with Cassini mosaic and radial-height lens.

sources.title: PSI Phoebe calibrated image collection
sources.evidence: Calibrated regional color candidates exist; projected RED product uses an ellipsoid and needs registration against the rendered shape. Does not establish global color coverage.

sources.title: Fraser and Brown 2018 Phoebe surface ice
sources.evidence: VIMS study provides spatial scientific interpretation, but this pass did not establish a released numeric projection/validity raster usable as a lens.

sources.title: Hedman et al. 2024 JWST Saturn small moon spectra
sources.evidence: Data-availability link resolves to authors released numeric spectra and processing. Disk-integrated spectra do not locate composition on the surface.
sources.scope: Epimetheus, Pandora, Telesto, Pallene; Cassini Methone comparison

sources.title: JWSTGiantPlanets SaturnRingsMoons released spectra
sources.evidence: Read README, four dither1 CSV files and Methone text data. CSV columns are wavelength, flux in Jy and error in Jy. Actual files have target-dependent useful wavelength limits. Methone data are Cassini VIMS, not JWST.

sources.title: Epimetheus released JWST spectrum
sources.evidence: Read 730 data rows; wavelength 1.351–4.999 microns, flux/error in Jy. Some samples noisy; do not turn negative flux into physical absence.

sources.title: Pallene released JWST spectrum
sources.evidence: Read 860 data rows; wavelength 0.700–4.999 microns, flux/error in Jy. Some samples noisy; do not turn negative flux into physical absence.

sources.title: Pandora released JWST spectrum
sources.evidence: Read 700 data rows; wavelength 1.501–4.999 microns, flux/error in Jy. Some samples noisy; do not turn negative flux into physical absence.

sources.title: Telesto released JWST spectrum
sources.evidence: Read 860 data rows; wavelength 0.700–5.000 microns, flux/error in Jy. Some samples noisy; do not turn negative flux into physical absence.

sources.title: Belyakov and Brown 2025 irregular Saturn moon JWST spectroscopy
sources.evidence: Target observations and archive DOI are explicit; wavelength-resolved disk-integrated composition, not spatial maps.

sources.title: MAST irregular Saturn moon observations
sources.evidence: Paper identifies released MAST program 3716 observations. DOI landing was unresolved during this pass; processed numeric-spectrum closure remains unverified.

sources.title: Brown et al. 2025 Saturn satellite carbon dioxide spectroscopy
sources.evidence: Eight exact targets in Table 1; hemisphere-integrated spectra and band measurements, not a global composition raster.
sources.scope: Mimas, Enceladus, Tethys, Dione, Rhea, Hyperion, Iapetus, Phoebe

sources.title: MAST Saturn major satellite CO2 observations
sources.evidence: Paper explicitly gives archive DOI, programs 3716 and Enceladus 1250. DOI landing not resolved here; retrieval/reduction not qualified.
sources.scope: Mimas, Enceladus, Tethys, Dione, Rhea, Hyperion, Iapetus, Phoebe

sources.title: Denk Ymir Cassini ISS numeric lightcurves
sources.evidence: Read numeric phase/lightcurve pairs grouped by named Cassini sequences; supports a measured photometry chart, not a texture.

sources.title: Denk linked native Ymir shape endpoint
sources.evidence: Fresh request returned HTTP 404. Existing authored approximate model must not be described as this native inversion mesh.

sources.title: Spitale and Porco 2010 outer B-ring observations
sources.evidence: Reports a compact shadow-casting body approximately 0.3 km across in the outer B ring. This observation is not a measured 3-axis shape or a current ephemeris.

limitations: This completes a bounded per-body source-feasibility review, not package qualification. No source baking, runtime fit, browser visual comparison, build, test or PR was performed.

Catalog and ephemeris inventories change and disagree at their publication boundaries. The frozen input has 293 Saturn rows; actual SAT459/SAT480 comments resolve the documented omissions without expanding the input.

All 231 rows with an MPEC reference were matched in all 96 distinct actual notices. Other rows retain JPL IAU/IAUC references and body-specific physical/mission evidence; inaccessible or unqueried IAU circular text is not represented as read.

The 122-irregular physical table has exact entries for 122 input bodies, leaving 146 irregular discoveries outside its scope. These rows were individually reconciled against discovery/ephemeris identifiers and the checked Cassini/shape product scope; this does not prove that no later observation exists.

Every one of the 35 missing named moons received an individual author-page review; 25 total Cassini Table 3 members and all 28 existing package source/recipe/content/manifest choices were inspected. Some author estimated size/pole fields differ from publications; explicit table identity governs reported ratios and periods.

Only metadata/small papers/numeric tables were retrieved. Tethys/Dione global subdirectory HTTP 403, Ymir native OBJ HTTP 404, Hyperion 2025 release identity and some MAST DOI resolutions remain concrete limits. Rhea actual OBJ names and small-moon numeric spectra were verified.

No minimum axis ratio is assigned to Narvi or Kari. Lightcurve inversion constraints, approximate inferred shapes, mean/photometric radii, measured ellipsoids and native released meshes remain separate.

Disk-integrated JWST spectra and Cassini lightcurves justify scientific charts or observation narratives, not spatial-color/composition textures. Spectral numeric units, uncertainties and wavelength cuts require implementation qualification.

No published global color-filled Titan composite is promoted as fully observed. Sparse Titan topography and its interpolation are separate products; Iapetus/Enceladus forthcoming SPC announcements are not releases.
Source SPK time coverage is a file interval, not an accuracy claim. SAT415 ends in 2018; package-specific fitted previews and historical pole conventions must not inherit broad source validity.
